You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — implement it end-to-end, including the parts not explicitly called out but implied (tests, wiring into existing UI/state, updating docs where load-bearing).

Goal: Project Page - Dynamic Build from Template Gallery

I'm building the template gallary right now on the Claude-Design-MCP. Your job would be to prepare the Session-Manager's Project Home page to be the visualization vehicle of these and to be build dynamically per Project 

Design a Project Page  (the current view) is one example that has a togle to switch display between 3 views - Marketing Landing Page - Feature Description Page- Architecture Overview Page These pages are going to be templates that our Agent is going to populate. Your job is to design the 3 pages whici are speaking about the project but from a different lens. Treat each Page a composable template and showcase 3 version of each page along 3-4 version for each compoenent. What you are building is a library of options, components that fit general set of "Projects"; What our Session Manager application will do is run an Agent to gather details from the current plroject, select the best fitting templates and populate the 3 pages

## Summary

Built the Project Page template gallery on top of the existing Project Home ("The Brief") tab:

**New files:**
- `src/renderer/lib/projectPageContent.ts` — `ProjectPageContent` schema + `deriveProjectPageContent(brief, projectName)`, a pure read-only derivation from the existing `ProjectBrief` (no fabricated copy, no new backend/IPC).
- `src/renderer/components/tabs/projecthome/pagegallery/blocks.tsx` — 7 composable block types (Hero, StatStrip, FeatureGrid, ArchitectureBlocks, Timeline, ConventionsPanel, CtaBanner), each with 3-4 distinct visual variants (28 total variants).
- `.../pagegallery/templates.tsx` — the template library: 9 fixed compositions, 3 per lens (Marketing Landing / Feature Description / Architecture Overview), each picking a variant per block.
- `.../pagegallery/ProjectPageGallery.tsx` — the toggle UI: a 3-way `ViewTabs` lens switch plus a per-lens template picker, rendering the selected template against derived Brief content.
- Tests for both the content derivation and template-registry integrity (11 new tests, all passing).

**Wired in:** `ProjectHome.tsx` now renders `<ProjectPageGallery>` right after the live "What is in flight" block and before the existing detailed Brief sections — additive, nothing existing removed or restyled.

**Verified:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint:selectors`, and the full `npm run test:unit` (209 files / 1942 tests) all pass clean.

**Deliberately out of scope** (per your framing — "our app will [eventually] run an Agent to gather details... and select the best fitting template"): the automatic template-selection agent itself. Today the human picks lens + template via the toggle; the library/contract is in place for that agent to plug into later by producing a `ProjectPageContent` directly instead of going through `deriveProjectPageContent`.

Walk me though how would the contruction of the page for new Project home be done from start to finish (look for gaps) Assume we are going to have template of pages and components, they will be expressed as (1) Component LIbrayr Input (2) the currect project's summary (3) summary to component mappings and rendering it; The summary will be a json that will be computed and (3) is a process of picking the best layout from the contenat; I guess my question is how would you structure it so that the Project Home does look different between projects based on (1) and (2) variations. Make sure that the architecture is solid, the Project Home before the intial RUN of this will have an empty page and 'Generate Now' button that will build it all. Oh I got it the output MUST be HTML with the 3 pages, what way out Project Home is guaranteed to rended it!!!  The attachment is the Component Library (make sure you save it to access in Session-Manager-Operations) in addition we should consider eventually how to include something like this as optional install to the the Session Manager

## Saved

Decompressed and saved the attached Component Library to `session-manager-operations/design-mocks/project-pages-component-library/` — the original bundle (`Component-Library.bundle.html`, opens standalone in a browser) plus its 7 source files extracted to readable JSX under `source/`, plus a `README.md` explaining the shape and load order. It's a design-tool export (self-extracting bundle with gzip+base64 assets in a manifest), not hand-written JSX, so I unpacked it rather than leaving it opaque.

What it actually contains, which changes the shape of your question: **not** flat components — a **slot/variant/preset system**. Each of the 3 lenses is a stack of slots (Marketing has 8: hero, proof, tour, workflow, depth, faq, pillars, close), each slot has 3-4 variant components, and each page ships 3 named presets (fixed slot→variant picks, e.g. "Editorial" / "Product-led" / "Developer") plus a "custom" override state. The variant `note` strings are literally selection hints in prose ("Needs a real quote", "Best for technical readers") — that's your future selection algorithm's raw material, just not yet machine-checkable.

## Architecture walkthrough — 4 stages, with the gaps

**Stage 0 — Component Library (build-time asset).** Today it's a browser-side-Babel bundle reading Google Fonts. That's fine for a design preview, wrong to ship: it violates the app's own "no network egress" architecture principle and re-transforms JSX in-browser on every render. Port it to real `.tsx` source, precompile once with esbuild into a pure function: `renderProjectPages(summary, picks) → { marketing: string, feature: string, architecture: string }` — plain `ReactDOMServer.renderToStaticMarkup` output, fonts self-hosted as local assets, zero runtime JSX transform.

**Stage 1 — Project Summary (your input #2, computed per-project).** **This is the biggest gap — it doesn't exist yet.** The library's `PROJ` shape (stats, pillars, quotes, one feature deep-dive with steps/rules/specs/faq/timeline, architecture layers/modules/flow/decisions/risks) is a strict superset of the current `ProjectBrief` (`purpose/what/areas/scope/conventions` only). You need a new synthesis pass — but it can build incrementally on top of an already-generated Brief rather than re-reading the repo from scratch (areas → pillars/modules, most-active Epic → the one feature spec, conventions → principles). Same cost-gated `claude -p` pattern as Brief refresh: manual trigger only, model-pinned, hard timeout.

**Stage 2 — Summary → Component mapping (your input #3, "picking the best layout").** Doesn't exist either. Formalize each variant's prose `note` into a checkable predicate (`requires: ['quotes.length>0']`, `avoidIf: ['screenshots.length===0']`), then a deterministic scorer per slot — no LLM call needed for a first cut, since nondeterministic re-layout on every regenerate is worse UX than a boring, repeatable rule. Persist the resulting picks (`picks.json`) so a regenerate doesn't silently reshuffle a layout the user already liked — mirrors Brief's pin mechanic, but pinning here is per-slot-pick, not per-paragraph-text.

**Stage 3 — Render + guaranteed display.** Your instinct is right: output MUST be static HTML files on disk, and Project Home hosts them in a **sandboxed iframe** (`srcDoc`), never re-composes them through the app's own React tree. That's what "guaranteed to render" actually buys you — the generated page is immune to the app's own React/Tailwind version ever changing underneath it. Empty state: no `output/*.html` yet → centered "Generate Now" button, same visual pattern as today's "no brief yet" state. Click → runs Stages 1-3 → writes 3 HTML files + a manifest (`generatedAt`, drift vs. Brief) → iframe renders them, toggle switches which file is shown.

## Gaps worth flagging explicitly
1. **No summary schema/synthesis** (Stage 1) — needs its own design pass before anything else can run.
2. **Selection algorithm unspecified** (Stage 2) — the `note` strings need formalizing into structured predicates.
3. **Storage/ownership undecided** — this needs a new `OWNERS` namespace (`project-pages`, writer `project-home`), same concurrency class as `brief.json` — Generate/Regenerate is an app-triggered write with a real double-click race, unlike the no-OWNERS `design-mocks/`/`HUMAN_LEARN/` folders.
4. **Screenshots** — several variants need real app screenshots (`FvShot` placeholders); the existing `blog-for-project-feature` skill already has a real-capture pipeline worth reusing rather than inventing a second one.
5. **Conflict with what I built earlier this session** — the `pagegallery/` work (live React composition from Brief, 9 fixed templates, no persisted static output) I shipped a few turns ago is the *wrong shape* for this ask: it recomposes live in the renderer instead of generating static HTML once. It's a reasonable prototype of the visual language but should be treated as superseded, not extended — worth an explicit decision before more work lands on top of it.

## Optional install (future)
Package Stage 0 (the compiled `renderProjectPages` bundle + fonts + slot/preset manifest) as an installable "design pack," same precedent as `pluginInstall.cjs`'s `claude plugin install <slug>` pattern already in this codebase — core app ships with none of the Almanac opinions baked in, a pack supplies the whole visual system, and Stages 1-2 (summary + selection) stay pack-agnostic. Bigger lift (needs a pack registry/discovery surface) — roadmap item, not now.

## Summary

**Reverted** the earlier live-composition MVP (`pagegallery/`, `projectPageContent.ts`, `ProjectHome.tsx` edits, CLAUDE.md addition) per your call that it wasn't needed and only the provided library should drive this.

**Built the infrastructure the feature hangs off of:**
- `session-manager-operations/architecture/project-pages-pipeline.md` — canonical spec for the 4-stage pipeline (I corrected one real mistake while writing it: I'd originally designed `project-pages/` as an `OWNERS` namespace like `brief.json`, but since generation runs as an Epic session writing with its own `Write` tool — not through `config.cjs` — the app's `assertOpsWrite` guard literally can't enforce that. Fixed: it's agent-authored artifact output, same class as `design-mocks/`/`HUMAN_LEARN/`, with concurrency handled by "Generate Now" resuming an already-active Epic instead of a filesystem lock).
- `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` — the registered local agent, pointing at the spec as source of truth.
- New Epic tag `project-home-builder` (`tagLibrary.ts`, `agentTagDefs.ts` with a full grounding `initialPromptTemplate`, `ticketDisplay.ts` chip tone, plus the two IPC-boundary copies of the tag union in `api.d.ts`/`ipcSchemas.cjs` that TypeScript caught) — following the existing `build` tag's soft-launch precedent: registered so `agentTagDef()` stays total, deliberately not yet in `AGENT_TAG_ORDER` since no creation UI exists until PRD 932 lands.
- Verified: `typecheck`, `lint:selectors`, and the full `test:unit` suite (208 files, 1941 tests) all green.

**Queued the build** via `/develop` inside this Epic (`psess-msbb6ipr-14`), as a 4-PRD dependency chain:
- **929** `project-pages-static-renderer` — ports the saved library into typed `.tsx`, builds the esbuild-compiled `renderProjectPages()` static-HTML renderer + CLI wrapper.
- **930** `project-pages-summary-schema` (deps: 929) — validated `ProjectPageSummary` contract + the `project-pages/README.md` documenting it as agent-authored, not OWNERS.
- **931** `project-pages-selection-scorer` (deps: 929, 930) — deterministic slot-selection scorer from the library's own variant `note` hints, plus idempotent `picks.json` merging.
- **932** `project-home-project-pages-ui` (deps: 929) — Project Home's empty state, "Generate Now"/"Regenerate" (creates-or-resumes the Epic), the new read-only `projectPages:get` IPC, and the sandboxed-iframe display.

These will drain through the scheduler in the background (billing-window-gated, ≤3 concurrent) — not something this turn can wait out. Check progress via the Scheduler tab or `scheduler_list_jobs`.
